mainTopic: Whether רבי מאיר holds that הקדש used by mistake stays holy, and testing the 'given for benefit' exception against his rulings on מעילה
overview: The משנה said in the name of רבי מאיר that a man who is מקדש a woman with הקדש succeeds only if he did it on purpose, not by mistake. Here the גמרא says that is not רבי מאיר's general rule for הקדש. The משנה is really about one special item: בגדי כהונה that are still wearable. Since the כהנים were allowed to benefit from them, using them by mistake is not מעילה. A ברייתא about worn-out garments is brought as a challenge, and the גמרא answers that it means only worn-out ones. Next come two sources where רבי מאיר holds there is מעילה even with things people cannot help benefiting from: the leftover funds of the לשכה, which pay for the city walls, and fallen stones of ירושלים. Each time the גמרא answers by switching the name to רבי יהודה. Then the גמרא objects that רבי יהודה seems to hold ירושלים is not holy at all, based on his view about vows using 'ירושלים' or 'like ירושלים'. The גמרא deals with this challenge on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי מאיר never holds that unwitting use fails to desacralize
steps.stepSummary: After checking all of רבי מאיר's teachings, the speaker found no general rule that הקדש stays holy when used בשוגג but loses its holiness when used במזיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: We looked at every side of רבי מאיר's opinions, and we never found him saying that holy property does not lose its holiness when used by mistake, but does lose it when used on purpose.
steps.whatsHappening: The speaker states that the rule the משנה seems to put in רבי מאיר's mouth (on purpose works, by mistake doesn't) is not his general view about הקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, using הקדש by mistake is מעילה, and that is exactly what takes the item out of its holiness. Using it on purpose is not מעילה, so it stays holy. Our משנה seemed to say the reverse in the name of רבי מאיר, and this statement says he does not hold that reverse rule for הקדש in general.

keyTerms.meaning: We went over every angle; we checked everything
Property set aside for the בית המקדש
By mistake, without knowing
On purpose, knowingly
Loses its holy status and becomes regular property

steps.confusionAlert: It sounds backwards, but with הקדש it is the mistaken use (מעילה) that takes the item out of holiness. Keep this in mind for the whole סוגיא.

phrases.english: We went around all the sides
of Rabbi Meir,
and we did not find consecrated property
that when used unwittingly is not desacralized,
but when used intentionally is desacralized.

steps.triggerLanguage: חָזַרְנוּ עַל כׇּל צְדָדִים שֶׁל רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion of the משנה about being מקדש with הקדש
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר has no general rule that הקדש used בשוגג stays holy while הקדש used במזיד loses its holiness.

steps.title: The משנה is about priestly garments that are still usable
steps.stepSummary: The משנה refers only to בגדי כהונה that have not worn out. Since כהנים were allowed to benefit from them, mistaken use is not מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה is talking about priestly tunics that are not yet worn out. They were given on the understanding that the כהנים may benefit from them, because the תורה was not given to angels.
steps.whatsHappening: The speaker explains how our משנה can still be רבי מאיר: it speaks about one special case, not about הקדש in general.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בגדי כהונה were given with permission for the כהנים to benefit from them, since no person can wear them only during the עבודה and never otherwise. So using them by mistake is not מעילה and does not take them out of holiness. If the woman was not betrothed בשוגג, it is because of this exception, not because of a general rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה, the one we are discussing
The tunics worn by the כהנים during the עבודה
Worn out, no longer usable
To benefit from
The ministering angels

steps.whyThisMatters: This reading lets the משנה stay in line with רבי מאיר's normal view of הקדש by treating בגדי כהונה as a special exception.

phrases.english: And our Mishnah is about priestly tunics
that have not worn out,
since they were given to be benefited from,
because the Torah was not given
to the ministering angels.
phrases.notes: People aren't angels; a כהן can't take the clothes off the second the עבודה ends.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the משנה fits with the statement in step 1
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Our משנה refers to unworn בגדי כהונה. Mistaken use of them is not מעילה because benefit from them was permitted from the start.

steps.title: Challenge from a ruling on worn-out priestly tunics
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says רבי מאיר holds there is מעילה with worn-out בגדי כהונה. Perhaps that means even unworn ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: with priestly tunics that wore out, one commits מעילה; this is רבי מאיר's view. Doesn't that mean even if they did not wear out?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge step 2's claim that רבי מאיר holds there is no מעילה with unworn בגדי כהונה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suggestion is that the ברייתא mentions worn-out garments to say that even they have מעילה, and unworn ones surely do. If so, mistaken use of unworn garments would be מעילה and would take them out of holiness, and step 2's explanation falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear; introduces a source as proof or challenge
One is guilty of מעילה, misusing holy property
Isn't it that...? Suggests a reading that creates a problem

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Priestly tunics that have worn out,
one commits misuse of consecrated property with them,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
Is it not so that this applies even if they have not worn out?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: כׇּתְנוֹת כְּהוּנָּה שֶׁבָּלוּ מוֹעֲלִין בָּהֶם
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that unworn בגדי כהונה have no מעילה according to רבי מאיר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי מאיר says there is מעילה even with worn-out garments, he probably means unworn ones too. Then mistaken use of unworn garments would be מעילה.

steps.title: Only worn-out garments
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the inference: the ברייתא speaks only about worn-out garments.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is only about garments that actually wore out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends step 2 by reading the ברייתא narrowly: it is talking only about worn-out tunics.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the garments are worn out, the כהנים can no longer use them, so the permission to benefit from them ends. Then they are like any other הקדש, with מעילה. Unworn garments, which are still in use, keep the permission and have no מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: Specifically, exactly; only this case

steps.whatToRemember: Unworn בגדי כהונה have no מעילה because using them was allowed. Worn-out ones go back to being regular הקדש with מעילה.

phrases.english: No, specifically ones that have worn out.

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the reading that the ברייתא includes unworn garments
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא's words 'שבלו' are meant exactly, not as a 'how much more so'.

steps.title: Another source: רבי מאיר on old shekels and leftover chamber funds
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא: רבי יהודה says there is מעילה with new שקלים but not old ones. רבי מאיר says even old ones, since he holds there is מעילה even with the leftovers of the לשכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: one commits מעילה with new שקלים but not with old ones, says רבי יהודה. רבי מאיר says even with old ones, because רבי מאיר used to say there is מעילה even with the leftover funds of the chamber.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a second challenge by quoting a ברייתא about רבי מאיר and מעילה. This step only sets up the source; the point of the challenge comes right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר is shown to be strict about מעילה: it applies even to money that is not going to buy קרבנות, like old שקלים and the leftover funds of the לשכה. The גמרא will use this strictness to test step 2's claim that unworn בגדי כהונה have no מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: New ones (here, this year's שקלים)
Old ones (here, שקלים from an earlier year)
The money left in the chamber after funds were taken out to buy communal קרבנות

phrases.english: Come and hear:
One commits misuse with new ones
phrases.notes: New and old שקלים: the half-שקל coins given this year versus ones given late for an earlier year.

phrases.english: but one does not commit misuse with old ones.
These are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.
Rabbi Meir says:
One commits misuse even with old ones,
for Rabbi Meir used to say:
One commits misuse with the leftovers of the chamber.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: מוֹעֲלִים בְּחַדְתִין וְאֵין מוֹעֲלִים בְּעַתִּיקִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first challenge was answered, the גמרא brings a new source about רבי מאיר and מעילה
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation of רבי מאיר's view in steps 1 and 2
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The source shows רבי מאיר applies מעילה very widely, even to שירי הלשכה. The next step (step 6) spells out why this clashes with the 'given for benefit' reasoning of step 2.

steps.title: The city walls are paid for from the leftover funds, and everyone benefits from them
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי מאיר holds there is מעילה with שירי הלשכה. The city walls are built from those funds, and people cannot avoid benefiting from them. So they should count as 'given for benefit' and carry no מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But why? Let us say: since they were given for people to benefit from, because the תורה was not given to angels. For the city wall and its towers are paid for from the leftovers of the chamber, as the משנה says: the city wall, its towers, and all the city's needs come from the leftovers of the chamber.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes the ברייתא from step 5 and turns it into a real challenge. It asks why רבי מאיר holds there is מעילה with the leftover funds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 2 we learned that בגדי כהונה carry no מעילה for mistaken use, because they were given so people could benefit from them. The leftover funds of the לשכה pay for the city walls, and people cannot help using the walls (walking by them, sheltering behind them). So by the same reasoning, רבי מאיר should hold that there is no מעילה with these funds.

keyTerms.meaning: But why? A question that opens a challenge
They were given on the understanding that people would benefit from them
The תורה was not given to angels. Its rules are made for real people with real limits
Leftover money in the בית המקדש treasury chamber after the year's offerings were bought
The wall of the city of ירושלים

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two ideas. The leftover funds are still הקדש. The question is only whether the 'given for benefit' rule removes מעילה from them.

phrases.english: But why?
phrases.notes: He means: why should רבי מאיר hold there is מעילה even with the old שקלים and the leftovers?

phrases.english: Let us say: since they were given to be benefited from

phrases.aramaic: לְפִי שֶׁלֹּא נִיתְּנָה תּוֹרָה לְמַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת
phrases.english: because the Torah was not given to the ministering angels
for the wall of the city and its towers
come from the leftovers of the chamber
as we learned: the wall of the city and its towers
and all the needs of the city
come from the leftovers of the chamber.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge from the ברייתא quoted in step 5 by explaining what is wrong with it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim (step 2) that רבי מאיר holds no מעילה for things given for benefit
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שירי הלשכה pay for the walls, which people cannot avoid benefiting from. So they are 'given for benefit', yet רבי מאיר holds there is מעילה with them.

steps.title: Switch the names: the opinion is רבי יהודה's
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the names in the ברייתא should be switched. The one who holds there is מעילה even with old שקלים and the leftovers is רבי יהודה, not רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do not say רבי מאיר; say רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by switching the names of the two תנאים in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the names are switched, רבי מאיר becomes the one who says there is no מעילה with old שקלים. That fits his view that things given for benefit carry no מעילה. The strict view about the leftovers now belongs to רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not say (read it this way)
Rather, say (read it that way). Used to switch the wording or the names in a teaching

phrases.english: Do not say רבי מאיר,
rather, say רבי יהודה.
phrases.notes: The גמרא is switching the names in the teaching about old שקלים from step 5.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא תֵּימָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר, אֶלָּא אֵימָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Switching the names of the תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא assigns the strict view about the leftovers to רבי מאיר.
steps.terutzMaskana: The strict view belongs to רבי יהודה, so רבי מאיר's view (no מעילה with things given for benefit) stays consistent.

steps.title: A second challenge: fallen stones of ירושלים
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי מאיר as saying there is מעילה with stones that fell from ירושלים. People benefit from those walls, so this again seems to contradict the 'given for benefit' rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: It was taught that רבי ישמעאל בר רבי יצחק said: stones of ירושלים that fell off, there is מעילה with them. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another source that seems to show רבי מאיר holds there is מעילה even with things people benefit from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The walls of ירושלים were built from הקדש funds, and people benefit from them all the time. If רבי מאיר still says there is מעילה with their fallen stones, then he does not seem to accept the 'given for benefit' rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear. Introduces a source brought as a proof or a challenge
The stones of ירושלים (from its walls and towers)
That fell off
One is liable for מעילה (misusing הקדש)

phrases.english: Come and hear: as it was taught,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בַּר רַבִּי יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: רבי ישמעאל בר רבי יצחק said:
stones of ירושלים that fell off
one is liable for מעילה with them,
the words of רבי מאיר.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: דְּתַנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בַּר רַבִּי יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new source raising the same kind of challenge as step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי מאיר holds no מעילה for things given for benefit
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: People benefit from the walls of ירושלים, yet רבי מאיר is quoted as holding there is מעילה with their stones.

steps.title: Again, switch the names to רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives the same answer as before: in this ברייתא, read רבי יהודה instead of רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do not say רבי מאיר; say רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the second challenge the same way it answered the first, by switching the name in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling that there is מעילה with the fallen stones now belongs to רבי יהודה. That keeps רבי מאיר's view consistent once again.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who, after the switch, holds the strict view about מעילה

phrases.english: Do not say רבי מאיר,
rather, say רבי יהודה.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא תֵּימָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר, אֶלָּא אֵימָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Switching the name of the תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ruling about the fallen stones is רבי מאיר's.

steps.title: According to רבי יהודה, is ירושלים holy at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the answer of step 9. A משנה about vows shows that רבי יהודה does not seem to treat ירושלים as holy. If so, how could he hold there is מעילה with its stones?
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is רבי יהודה, is ירושלים holy? But we learned: 'like the lamb, like the pens, like the wood, like the fires, like the היכל, like the מזבח, like ירושלים.' רבי יהודה says: anyone who says 'ירושלים' has not said anything.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the name switch it just made. It quotes a משנה showing that רבי יהודה seems not to view ירושלים as holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A vow works by comparing an item to something holy. רבי יהודה says that someone who vows using 'ירושלים' has said nothing, which suggests ירושלים is not holy in his view. If ירושלים is not holy, its stones cannot carry מעילה, so the ruling about the stones cannot be his.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it holy? (a question asked as a challenge)
But didn't we learn in a משנה?
The lamb (of the daily offering)
Pens where animals set aside as offerings were kept
The fires on the מזבח
He has said nothing. His words have no legal effect

phrases.english: If it is רבי יהודה,
is ירושלים holy?
But we learned: 'like the lamb, like the pens, like the wood,'
phrases.notes: These are ways of making a vow: a person says an item is forbidden to him 'like' one of these holy things.

phrases.english: 'like the fires, like the Sanctuary, like the altar, like ירושלים.'
רבי יהודה says:
anyone who says 'ירושלים' has not said anything.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, יְרוּשָׁלַיִם מִי מִיקַּדְּשָׁא? וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 9 by showing a problem with assigning the ruling to רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The switch in step 9 that gives the fallen-stones ruling to רבי יהודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה says a vow using 'ירושלים' has no effect, which suggests ירושלים is not holy. Then its stones could not carry מעילה in his view.
steps.whyThisMatters: If this challenge stands, the name switch fails, and רבי מאיר is again left holding a view that clashes with step 2.

steps.title: It is not just about the wording 'like ירושלים'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא blocks a possible way out: maybe רבי יהודה rejected the vow only because the person said 'ירושלים' instead of 'like ירושלים'. A ברייתא shows that רבי יהודה rejects even 'like ירושלים', unless the vow refers to something offered in ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say it is because he did not say 'like ירושלים': but it was taught that רבי יהודה says: anyone who says 'like ירושלים' has not said anything, until he vows by something that is offered in ירושלים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a possible answer to its own challenge and then knocks it down with a ברייתא. This makes the challenge of step 10 stronger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think רבי יהודה only objected to the wording 'ירושלים' without 'like'. The ברייתא shows he rejects even 'like ירושלים'. A vow works for him only when it refers to something offered as a קרבן there. So in רבי יהודה's view, ירושלים itself really does seem not to be holy.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say. Introduces a possible answer that is about to be rejected
But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא?
Until he makes his vow
Something that is offered as a קרבן

phrases.english: And if you will say,
it is because he did not say: 'like ירושלים',
phrases.notes: In the משנה of step 10, the person said just 'ירושלים', without the word 'like'.

phrases.english: but it was taught: רבי יהודה says:
anyone who says 'like ירושלים' has not said anything,
until he vows by something that is offered in ירושלים!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא, מִשּׁוּם דְּלֹא אָמַר: ״כִּירוּשָׁלַיִם״, וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Makes the challenge of step 10 stronger by closing off a possible answer about the vow's wording.
steps.kashyaTarget: The possible defense that רבי יהודה rejected the vow only because of its wording
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה rejects even 'like ירושלים' and accepts only a vow by something offered there. So he really does seem to hold that ירושלים itself is not holy.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggested answer that the problem was only the missing word 'like'
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא explicitly shows that the full wording 'like ירושלים' also has no effect for רבי יהודה.
steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא moved the strict rulings (leftover funds, fallen stones) from רבי מאיר to רבי יהודה. But רבי יהודה seems to hold that ירושלים is not holy at all, so the fallen-stones ruling is hard to give to him. The גמרא deals with this challenge on the next amud.
